paper.title: Utility Fairness in Contextual Dynamic Pricing with Demand Learning

settings.name_in_paper: Fair contextual pricing with incomplete information (demand learning under delta_0-utility fairness)
unmapped: Dynamic pricing: action is a contextual pricing policy pi: X -> [p_low, p_high]; demand E[y|x,p] = f(x^T theta_0 - alpha_0 p) with known link f (generalized linear demand), revenue p*y
Policies must satisfy delta_0-utility fairness: |pi(x)-pi(x')| <= delta_0 |(x-x')^T theta_0|; regret measured against best delta_0-UF policy
Contexts i.i.d. with non-degenerate covariance (lambda_min >= sigma_x) and bounded density of utility
Smooth, strongly unimodal revenue curves; likelihood function satisfying regularity assumption
settings.definition_quote: We adopt a generalized linear model to model the probabilistic realizations of demands given customer contexts $x\in\mX\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ and offered price $p\in[\underline p,\overline p]$... $\mathbb E[y|x,p] = f(x^\top\theta_0-\alpha_0 p)$ ... A contextual pricing policy $\pi$ satisfies $\delta_0$-utility fairness if for any $x,x'$ it holds that $|\pi(x)-\pi(x')|\leq\delta_0|(x-x')^\top\theta_0|$.

algorithms.name: Contextual pricing with utility fairness constraints and demand learning (Algorithm 1: price experimentation + MLE + UCB over discretized starting prices)
requires_knowledge_of: kappa_1 depends on M_r, diam(X), sigma_x, sigma_r

conditions: algorithm implements delta_0-UF policies with probability >= 0.95 for all instances

source.label: thm:lower-bound
source.quote: Fix arbitrary $\delta_0\in(0,1/2]$ and let $\underline C>0$ be a strictly positive constant potentially depending on $\delta_0$. Let $f(u)\equiv u$ be the purely linear demand model. There exists model set-up ... such that, for any contextual pricing with demand learning algorithm ... if such an algorithm satisfies $\Pr[\pi_1,\cdots,\pi_T\in\mF_{\theta_0,\alpha_0}(\delta_0)] \geq 0.95$, then $\sup \mathbb E[\sum_t \max_{\pi}R(\pi)-R(\pi_t)]\geq \underline C\times T^{2/3}$

results.notes: Proof sets underline C = delta_0^{2/3}/123. Regret defined via expected revenues of policies (pseudo-regret). Algorithm class: algorithms that are fair w.p. >= 0.95.

conditions: Assumptions 1-5 (boundedness, smooth strongly unimodal revenue, stochastic contexts, non-degenerate covariance, likelihood regularity)
delta_0 <= sigma_u/M_r so the optimal UF policy is linear

source.label: thm:upper-bound
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions \ref{asmp:boundedness}-\ref{asmp:likelihood} hold, and $\delta_0\leq\sigma_u/M_r$ ... With probability $1-\tilde O(T^{-2})$, the following hold: (Fairness) All $\pi_1,\cdots,\pi_T$ satisfy $\delta_0$-utility fairness ... (Regret) $\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbb E_{x\sim P_{\mX}}[r_x(\pi^*(x))-r_x(\pi_t(x))]\leq (6L_f\tilde B\kappa_1 + 4L_f\kappa_2) T^{2/3}$

results.notes: Effectively O~(T^{2/3}) since kappa_1, kappa_2 contain sqrt(log) factors. Also guarantees all policies are delta_0-UF w.h.p. Regret is sum of expected (over context) revenue gaps of realized policies, holding w.h.p.
